title: Behavior-driven PRD and progressive launch orchestration for hosted inference endpoints
creator: Marcus Chen
description: This PRD captures explicit behavioral contracts and acceptance gates for the four hosted inference surfaces (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank) plus an orchestration checklist for progressive launch. The goal is to (1) define unambiguous API behaviour and backward compatibility expectations, (2) enumerate SLOs and quality metrics to gate rollout, and (3) provide an operational checklist for engineering/infra to follow during canary -> ramp -> GA. This doc is deliberately behavior-driven to ensure product, design, and engineering agree on what 'works' for customers before large-scale traffic switchovers.
acceptance_criteria: General: All endpoints must support existing REST/SDK contracts; any change requiring client updates must be opt-in and documented in the breaking-changes playbook.

Chat: Streaming tokens must be emitted in-order, with partial delta patches matching schema v2; total end-to-end median latency for 100-token responses must be <= 220ms in hosted-us-east region under normal load.

Completions: Non-streaming completion responses must include deterministic 'stop' handling; throughput (tokens/sec) for the default small model must meet or exceed baseline throughput captured in runtime-1.20 benchmarks.
Embeddings: Returned vectors must be fixed-dimension 1536 (where model requires) and average cosine similarity drift vs. evaluation goldset must be < 0.015 after quantization/optimization steps.
Rerank: Top-5 MRR on internal rerank testset must not regress by more than 1.5% relative to the staging baseline; ranking tie-handling must be stable across identical inputs.
Backward compatibility: SDKs using previous stable contract must continue to function for 90 days after release; deprecation notices must be published at least 30 days before removal.
Quality gates: No release to >10% user traffic unless all per-endpoint QA suites pass and automated evaluation shows no quality regression beyond thresholds.
Telemetry: Every request must emit route, model_variant, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, response_code, cache_hit boolean, and kv_cache_size tags for downstream alerts and cost allocation.
launch_checklist: Pre-launch: finalize API surface doc and update SDK changelog entries (confluence link in links).
Pre-launch: run synthetic traffic sweep (10k reqs/hour) for 72 hours across hosts and collect latencies and error rates.
Infra: confirm autoscaling policies and warm GPU pools for reserved capacity customers.
Security: complete KMS/HSM integration verification for Private tenants and confirm audit logging enabled.
Observability: dashboards deployed for per-route cost/latency, and trace sampling enabled for 100% of canary traffic.
QA: end-to-end tests for function calling, structured output, and streaming semantics green.
Docs: publish API migration notes, examples for streaming and streaming->non-streaming fallback, and embed dimensional guarantees.
Stakeholders: product/engineering/ops/solutions engineering sign-off recorded in decisions_log.
Rollout: begin canary at 1% traffic for 24 hours, then 5% for 48 hours, 25% for 72 hours, then 100% if all gates pass.
Post-launch: run 14-day correctness monitoring and schedule regression review in week 2 and week 4.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Internal Staging): simulate 3 production regions; collect goldset metrics and latency percentiles.
Phase 1 (Canary 1%): route only internal beta customers and automated test traffic; monitor heatmap for new error classes.
Phase 2 (Canary 5%): add low-risk external customers and monitor quality metrics (MRR, embedding cosine mean, BLEU-ish proxies) vs. baseline.
Phase 3 (Ramp 25%): evaluate cost regression and autoscale behavior under sustained load; verify fallback to previous model variant works within 30s.
Phase 4 (GA 100%): full traffic switch after two consecutive ramp windows pass with no open regressions.
telemetry_and_alerts: Primary SLOs: 99th percentile latency for 100-token chat responses < 1500ms; error rate < 0.3% per 5m window.
Quality sentinel: Embedding drift > 0.02 avg cosine delta triggers a quality-alert and automatic hold on rollout.
Cost sentinel: per-token cost increase > 18% relative to baseline triggers review and temporary rate-limit by tier.
Fallback alert: If canary error rate > 0.6% for 10 minutes or sustained latency > 2x baseline for 5 minutes, rollback should be executed automatically by infra runbook.
Operational logs: each rollback must create a postmortem ticket and link to the initiating alert.
qa_plan: Unit & integration: API contract tests for each endpoint with synthetic inputs covering edge-cases (stream truncation, interrupt, function call edge flows).
E2E: user-simulated flows for chat with stateful context up to 2048 tokens and verify KV cache behavior across shard boundaries.
Regression: run nightly goldset evaluation comparing new variant vs. staging baseline for embeddings and rerank.
Load: run progressive load test to exercise batching paths (small, medium, large batch profiles) and validate throughput curves.
Accessibility & Docs QA: sample SDKs and quickstarts executed in CI to ensure code examples compile and docs match behavior.
risks_mitigations: Risk: Quality regressions after quantization for embeddings. Mitigation: hold quantized variant behind feature-flag and ramp only with embedding-drift sentinel checks.
Risk: Streaming semantics drift causing client failures. Mitigation: maintain streaming compatibility mode and run SDK smoke tests against canary.
Risk: Autoscale thrash under bursty traffic. Mitigation: adjust cooldowns and provide temporary burst credit for Dedicated customers during ramp windows.
Risk: Unexpected cost spike due to changed batching. Mitigation: include cost sentinel and temporary per-tenant throttles that can be applied by SRE.
